ops.title: capt-hook 9.11.0 (2026-07-13) shipped Phase 2 of the perf pass — the opt-in resident per-project daemon (hookd) + stdlib thin client (hook), ~7x warm dispatch, byte-parity acceptance gate; dogfood flip deferred; Phase 3 = default-on rollout
ops.body:
capt-hook **9.11.0** (2026-07-13, tag v9.11.0 on f8175c50) = Phase 2 of the hard perf pass ([[perf-pass-phase1-shipped]] was Phase 1). Master plan `~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-07/plans/what-s-happening-1-cozy-candle.md`.

**Shipped**: opt-in resident per-project daemon. New top-level stdlib-only `capt_hook_client` package (`key.py` shared worker-key/paths contract, `client.py` thin forwarder). Binaries: **`hook`** = thin client (wired in the hook-command slot: `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.venv/bin/hook run <Event>`), **`hookd`** = daemon (`hookd run|status|stop|restart|logs`; `hookd = "captain_hook.cli:daemon"`, points at the existing hidden Click group — client's internal spawn stays `-m captain_hook daemon run`), **`capt-hook`** = fat CLI unchanged. `captain_hook/daemon/` package (protocol/registry/context/server/lifecycle/logsink/transcache/decision_writer). Measured **~70ms p50 warm vs ~490ms cold (~7x)**; 27-way storm → 1 worker. **Byte-parity is the contract** — 12-case acceptance gate (tests/test_daemon_parity.py) runs warm-vs-cold byte-identical under CAPT_HOOK_DAEMON_FALLBACK=closed. Cold fallback on any unavailability; **send-boundary rule**: pre-send failure → cold, post-send failure → fail-open (never double-fire); untrusted run dir → always cold.

**Key seams (pure refactors, keystones)**: `util/reqenv.py` (per-request env/cwd ContextVar, authoritative-for-whitelisted), `app.py` StateProxy (`_state` → ContextVar-scoped, zero test edits landed as the proof), `cli.py` `dispatch_event` split (claim_once stays in run_event, daemon calls it at its own front door). Once-guard sentinel moved to `resolve_cache_dir()/once` (XDG-based, TMPDIR-independent — was a real cross-session double-fire bug).

**Review was heavy and paid off**: mid-wave (codex finder+refuter) + final (finder/refuter/security) + a fix-verification pass + a round-2 for residual edges, each codex xhigh via the CLI. Real bugs caught+fixed: once-guard TMPDIR divergence, client fail-open-should-be-cold on pre-send failures, env_map leaking daemon env, registry torn-discovery TOCTOU, idle/restart dropping in-flight requests (missed denies), skip-perms consent-cache poisoning, a latent teardown DEADLOCK, log-mode-lost-on-rotation. codex moderation flags offensive-security phrasing ("attack/refuter/demonstrate") — reword to plain verification framing; pin `--sandbox workspace-write` + a scratch `-C` workdir (it silently defaulted to danger-full-access).

**Deferred to Phase 3** (recorded in the plan, MUST resolve before default-on): plugin `hooks.json` still cold `uvx --isolated capt-hook run` (consumers opt-in); wheel-upgrade daemon retirement (build_id churn-guard interaction); non-whitelisted secret isolation across pooled accounts (worker-sharing vs secret bleed — user design decision).

**Dogfood flip LANDED 2026-07-14** (96f2c16e on main): committed `.claude/settings.json` now runs `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.venv/bin/hook run <Event>` for all 12 events × sync+async; the two async `review run` lines stay on `capt-hook` (the client execv-passthroughs them anyway). Measured against this repo's REAL pack set (general/python/steering/fixes — note the `ccx` grep guard is NOT a capt-hook pack, it's the cc-context plugin): PreToolUse 581ms→**63ms**, PostToolUse 1833ms→**130ms**, byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit vs cold, exactly 1 worker under warm reuse, correct cold-fallback on `kill -9` and on `CAPT_HOOK_NO_DAEMON=1`. Gate gotchas: `CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR` is IN the worker key, so varying it per test case spawns a worker per case and you only ever exercise the cold-spawn path; and a run dir created with plain `mkdir` (0755) makes the client refuse the daemon and silently run cold ("unsafe mode 0755 (want 0700)"). Sync `.venv` (so `hook`/`hookd` exist) BEFORE the settings flip lands.

Process: concurrent sessions burn versions fast (9.4→9.11 in ~1 day) and race the shared checkout — pick the release number from PyPI at tag time (v9.11.0 grabbed after 9.10.0 released mid-wave), merge-not-rebase, CHANGELOG conflicts resolve newest-on-top. Two-writers-in-one-worktree is a hazard (docs agent re-activated into the rename agent's tree — benign only because the amend preceded the merge; verify via reflog).
